messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Mean Occupancy Estimate from occu()
parts:
Hi Alex,

I believe what you are looking to calculate are model averaged coefficients. This isn't currently available in unmarked, and I believe that is because the purpose of using occupancy models is not so much to calculate the values of coefficients, but to predict occupancy/abundance/detection probability across the range of your variables. However there are other packages which can be used to average your coefficients; just be careful about your interpretation of these values.

Someone with more experience might want to jump in here in case I'm way off track :)

Rachael 

On Tue, Sep 22, 2020 at 5:07 PM Alex Buckisch <alex.b...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi everyone,

I've been looking for a while trying to find an answer but am either blind or not asking the right questions...

I would like to get a mean occupancy estimate for a single-season, single-species model that uses multiple site-covariates.
I know how to backtransform from logit scale to original. But am unsure of how to get a single mean estimate from multiple betas.

Below is some of my code that may describe my question better (one observer-covariate for p, two site-covariates for psi):

# Top Model
fm6 <- occu(~Temp ~Elevation + Trails, data = ODVI_umf)

# Summary
# P-values < 0.05 suggest significant influence of site-covariates on occupancy probability
Call:
occu(formula = ~Temp ~Elevation + Trails, data = ODVI_umf)

Occupancy (logit-scale):
                    Estimate   SE    z       P(>|z|)
(Intercept)   -0.757 0.592 -1.28  0.2008
Elevation     -3.536 1.511 -2.34  0.0193
Trails             3.155 1.371  2.30  0.0214

Detection (logit-scale):
            Estimate    SE     z  P(>|z|)
(Intercept)   -1.773 0.321 -5.53 3.21e-08
Temp             0.755 0.275  2.74 6.14e-03

AIC: 133.4865 
Number of sites: 29
optim convergence code: 0
optim iterations: 20 
Bootstrap iterations: 0

# Backtransforming from logit to original scale
plogis(coef(fm6))

      psi(Int)          psi(Elevation)    psi(Trails)              p(Int)              p(Temp) 
    0.31927503     0.02831501     0.95910018     0.14518155     0.68020885  


This is where I struggle. Now I would just like to say: estimated mean occupancy for this species under the top model (fm6) was "VALUE".
Is it just as simple as (psi(Elevation) + psi(Trails)) / 2?

Thank you in advance! I am glad this forum is still active after all these years and offering an immensely helpful resource!

Alex

messages.subject: RE: [unmarked] Mean Occupancy Estimate from occu()
parts:
Alex,


If you are looking for the "mean occupancy" from your model, I think you need to step back a little and consider what you are looking for exactly. If your model has a number of covariates and you find that these covariates influence occupancy, then you should consider whether it is reasonable to get a "mean occupancy" and what it would actually mean. In your example, both elevation (-) and trails (+) influence occupancy: i.e., the model is suggesting that occupancy varies with elevation and trails.


If you consider it sensible to get a "mean occupancy" from a single model, then there would be a number of potential ways of doing so, namely

-running an intercept-only model for occupancy

-computing a prediction of occupancy by inserting the mean of each variable from your data set into the logit equation of occupancy

-computing a prediction of occupancy by inserting the mean of each variable from your study area into the logit equation of occupancy


To help you get further, note that you can find useful information on this forum in already posted threads.


Good luck,


Marc

messages.author: 4f80e1927b0757cb
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Mean Occupancy Estimate from occu()
parts:
Alex,

It depends on what the "mean" occupancy is supposed to represent. Here are a few possible options:

1) The expected occupancy probability at a theoretical "average" site with average values for each covariate
You can get this with the predict() function and supplying newdata:

predict(fm6, "state", newdata=data.frame(Elevation=mean(siteCovs(ODVI_umf)$Elevation, Trails=mean(siteCovs(ODVI_umf)$Trails))

2) The mean of the expected occupancies at each actual site
You can also get this with predict(). If you call it without newdata it will give you the expected occupancy probability at each site your dataset:

pr <- predict(fm6, "state")
mean(pr$Predicted)

3) The Empirical Bayes estimate of the "realized" proportion of sites occupied (the estimated mean of the latent occupancy state Z across sites).
You can get this with ranef() and bup().

re <- ranef(fm6)
mean(bup(re, stat="mode"))

See ?ranef and ?bup for more on the last one.

Ken
